# xsv - CSV Command Line Toolkit

**Note:** xsv is now unmaintained. Consider using [qsv](https://github.com/dathere/qsv) or [xan](https://github.com/medialab/xan) as alternatives.

## Overview

xsv is a command line program for indexing, slicing, analyzing, splitting and joining CSV files. Commands are designed to be simple, fast and composable.

## Available Commands

* **cat** - Concatenate CSV files by row or by column.
* **count** - Count the rows in a CSV file. (Instantaneous with an index.)
* **fixlengths** - Force a CSV file to have same-length records by either padding or truncating them.
* **flatten** - A flattened view of CSV records. Useful for viewing one record at a time. e.g., `xsv slice -i 5 data.csv | xsv flatten`.
* **fmt** - Reformat CSV data with different delimiters, record terminators or quoting rules. (Supports ASCII delimited data.)
* **frequency** - Build frequency tables of each column in CSV data. (Uses parallelism to go faster if an index is present.)
* **headers** - Show the headers of CSV data. Or show the intersection of all headers between many CSV files.
* **index** - Create an index for a CSV file. This is very quick and provides constant time indexing into the CSV file.
* **input** - Read CSV data with exotic quoting/escaping rules.
* **join** - Inner, outer and cross joins. Uses a simple hash index to make it fast.
* **partition** - Partition CSV data based on a column value.
* **sample** - Randomly draw rows from CSV data using reservoir sampling (i.e., use memory proportional to the size of the sample).
* **reverse** - Reverse order of rows in CSV data.
* **search** - Run a regex over CSV data. Applies the regex to each field individually and shows only matching rows.
* **select** - Select or re-order columns from CSV data.
* **slice** - Slice rows from any part of a CSV file. When an index is present, this only has to parse the rows in the slice (instead of all rows leading up to the start of the slice).
* **sort** - Sort CSV data.
* **split** - Split one CSV file into many CSV files of N chunks.
* **stats** - Show basic types and statistics of each column in the CSV file. (i.e., mean, standard deviation, median, range, etc.)
* **table** - Show aligned output of any CSV data using elastic tabstops.

## Usage Examples

### Viewing CSV Headers

```bash
$ xsv headers worldcitiespop.csv
1   Country
2   City
3   AccentCity
4   Region
5   Population
6   Latitude
7   Longitude
```

### Statistics Overview

Get an overview of data in each column:

```bash
$ xsv stats worldcitiespop.csv --everything | xsv table
```

### Selecting Columns

Select specific columns from a CSV file:

```bash
$ xsv select Country,AccentCity,Population worldcitiespop.csv | xsv table
```

### Searching with Regex

Search for rows matching a pattern:

```bash
$ xsv search -s Country '^US$' worldcitiespop.csv | xsv table
```

### Frequency Analysis

Build a frequency table for a column:

```bash
$ xsv frequency -s Country worldcitiespop.csv | xsv table
```

### Sampling Data

Randomly sample rows from a CSV file:

```bash
$ xsv sample 10 worldcitiespop.csv
```

### Sorting Data

Sort CSV data by a specific column:

```bash
$ xsv sort -s Population worldcitiespop.csv
```

### Joining CSV Files

Join two CSV files on a common column:

```bash
$ xsv join Country file1.csv Country file2.csv
```

### Slicing Rows

Extract specific rows from a CSV file:

```bash
$ xsv slice -s 10 -e 20 worldcitiespop.csv
```

### Counting Rows

Count the number of rows (extremely fast with an index):

```bash
$ xsv count worldcitiespop.csv
```

### Creating an Index

Create an index for faster operations:

```bash
$ xsv index worldcitiespop.csv
```

== /tmp/help_cat.txt ==
Concatenates CSV data by column or by row.

When concatenating by column, the columns will be written in the same order as
the inputs given. The number of rows in the result is always equivalent to to
the minimum number of rows across all given CSV data. (This behavior can be
reversed with the '--pad' flag.)

When concatenating by row, all CSV data must have the same number of columns.
If you need to rearrange the columns or fix the lengths of records, use the
'select' or 'fixlengths' commands. Also, only the headers of the *first* CSV
data given are used. Headers in subsequent inputs are ignored. (This behavior
can be disabled with --no-headers.)

Usage:
    xsv cat rows    [options] [<input>...]
    xsv cat columns [options] [<input>...]
    xsv cat --help

cat options:
    -p, --pad              When concatenating columns, this flag will cause
                           all records to appear. It will pad each row if
                           other CSV data isn't long enough.

Common options:
    -h, --help             Display this message
    -o, --output <file>    Write output to <file> instead of stdout.
    -n, --no-headers       When set, the first row will NOT be interpreted
                           as column names. Note that this has no effect when
                           concatenating columns.
    -d, --delimiter <arg>  The field delimiter for reading CSV data.
                           Must be a single character. (default: ,)

== /tmp/help_count.txt ==
Prints a count of the number of records in the CSV data.

Note that the count will not include the header row (unless --no-headers is
given).

Usage:
    xsv count [options] [<input>]

Common options:
    -h, --help             Display this message
    -n, --no-headers       When set, the first row will not be included in
                           the count.
    -d, --delimiter <arg>  The field delimiter for reading CSV data.
                           Must be a single character. (default: ,)

== /tmp/help_fixlengths.txt ==
Transforms CSV data so that all records have the same length. The length is
the length of the longest record in the data (not counting trailing empty fields,
but at least 1). Records with smaller lengths are padded with empty fields.

This requires two complete scans of the CSV data: one for determining the
record size and one for the actual transform. Because of this, the input
given must be a file and not stdin.

Alternatively, if --length is set, then all records are forced to that length.
This requires a single pass and can be done with stdin.

Usage:
    xsv fixlengths [options] [<input>]

fixlengths options:

contents of each field to provide a summary view.

// CSV parsing
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct CsvRecord {
    fields: Vec<String>,
    // raw bytes? For index we need byte offsets. But for parsing we need to handle quoted newlines.
}

struct CsvReader<R: Read> {
    reader: BufReader<R>,
    delimiter: u8,
    quote: u8,
    escape: Option<u8>,
    quoting: bool,
    // For tracking byte offset
    pos: u64,
    // buffer for line reading
    // We will implement a proper CSV parser that handles multiline quoted fields.
}

fn parse_csv<R: Read>(mut rdr: R, delimiter: u8, quote: u8, escape: Option<u8>, quoting: bool) -> Result<Vec<Vec<String>>, String> {
    // Read all bytes
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    rdr.read_to_end(&mut buf).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    parse_csv_bytes(&buf, delimiter, quote, escape, quoting)
}

fn parse_csv_bytes(data: &[u8], delimiter: u8, quote: u8, escape: Option<u8>, quoting: bool) -> Result<Vec<Vec<String>>, String> {
    let mut records: Vec<Vec<String>> = Vec::new();
    let mut field = Vec::new();
    let mut record: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    let len = data.len();
    let mut in_quote = false;
    let mut at_start_of_field = true;
    // For handling \r\n? We treat \n as newline, \r\n as newline, \r as newline? Original xsv uses csv crate which handles \r\n and \n.
    // Simplified: \r\n considered single newline if not inside quotes.
    // We'll parse according to RFC4180-ish.

    while i < len {
        let c = data[i];
        if in_quote {
            if let Some(esc) = escape {
                if c == esc {
                    // escape next char
                    if i+1 < len {
                        let next = data[i+1];
                        // Escape handling: if escape == quote, then escaping?
                        // Original: when escape specified, quotes escaped by escape char.
                        // We implement: if c == escape, then next char is taken literally (including quote or escape)
                        field.push(next);
                        i+=2;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    } else {
                        field.push(c);
                        i+=1;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                } else if c == quote {
                    // end quote? Check if next is quote (doubled)
                    // If escape is None, doubled quotes escape.
                    if escape.is_none() {
                        if i+1 < len && data[i+1]==quote {
                            field.push(quote);
                            i+=2;
                            at_start_of_field = false;
                            continue;
                        } else {
                            in_quote = false;
                            i+=1;
                            at_start_of_field = false;
                            continue;
                        }
                    } else {
                        // escape is Some, so quote ends unless escaped
                        in_quote = false;
                        i+=1;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                } else {
                    field.push(c);
                    i+=1;
                    at_start_of_field = false;
                    continue;
                }
            } else {
                // No escape char, double quote escaping
                if c == quote {
                    if i+1 < len && data[i+1]==quote {
                        field.push(quote);
                        i+=2;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    } else {
                        in_quote = false;
                        i+=1;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                } else {
                    field.push(c);
                    i+=1;
                    at_start_of_field = false;
                    continue;
                }
            }
        } else {
            // not in quote
            if quoting && at_start_of_field && c == quote {
                in_quote = true;
                i+=1;
                at_start_of_field = false;
                continue;
            }

        if in_quote {

                    if i+1 < len {
                        field.push(data[i+1]);

                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    } else {
                        field.push(c);
                        i+=1;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;

                    if escape.is_none() {

                        continue;
                    }

                    field.push(c);
                    i+=1;
                    at_start_of_field = false;
                    continue;
                }

                        continue;
                    } else {

                }

                i+=1;
                continue;

                field.clear();
                records.push(record.clone());

fn write_csv_record<W: Write>(writer: &mut W, fields: &[String], out_delim: u8, quote: u8, quote_always: bool, escape: Option<u8>, crlf: bool, ascii: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
    // ascii overrides delimiter and terminator?
    // According to spec: --ascii uses \x1F as field sep and \x1E as record sep.
    // From earlier od: fmt --ascii produced \x1F between fields, \x1E as record separator.
    // Indeed: "h1\x1Fh2\x1Fh3\x1Ea\x1Fb\x1Fc\x1E..."
    // So when ascii flag set, out_delim is 0x1F, record terminator 0x1E.
    // Quote handling with ascii? Our od showed quote-always with ascii produced quoted fields still with \x1F and \x1E inside? Actually earlier ascii with quote-always gave: 22 68 31 22 1f ... So fields quoted with ", then delimiter 0x1F etc.
    // So implement.

    let field_sep = if ascii { 0x1F } else { out_delim };
    let record_sep = if ascii { 0x1E } else { b'\n' };

    for (idx, field) in fields.iter().enumerate() {
        if idx > 0 {
            writer.write_all(&[field_sep])?;
        }
        // Determine if need quoting
        let needs_quote = if quote_always {
            true
        } else {
            // Need quote if field contains delimiter, quote, newline, \r, or if ascii? Check: ascii doesn't require quoting unless field contains sep or quote etc?
            // Also if field contains out_delim, quote, \r, \n, etc.
            let bytes = field.as_bytes();
            let mut need = false;
            for &b in bytes {
                if b == out_delim && !ascii { need = true; break; }
                if b == field_sep { need = true; break; }
                if b == record_sep { need = true; break; }
                if b == quote { need = true; break; }
                if b == b'\n' || b == b'\r' { need = true; break; }
            }
            need
        };

        if needs_quote {
            writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
            // escape
            for &b in field.as_bytes() {
                if b == quote {
                    if let Some(esc) = escape {
                        writer.write_all(&[esc])?;
                        writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
                    } else {
                        // double quote
                        writer.write_all(&[quote, quote])?;
                    }
                } else {
                    writer.write_all(&[b])?;
                }
            }
            writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
        } else {
            writer.write_all(field.as_bytes())?;
        }
    }
    if crlf && !ascii {
        writer.write_all(b"\r\n")?;
    } else {
        writer.write_all(&[record_sep])?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn csv_writer_from_path(path_opt: Option<&str>) -> Box<dyn Write> {
    if let Some(p) = path_opt {
        let f = File::create(p).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
            eprintln!("failed to open {}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", p);
            std::process::exit(1);
        });
        Box::new(BufWriter::new(f))
    } else {
        Box::new(BufWriter::new(io::stdout()))
    }
}

// Delimiter parsing
fn parse_delim(s: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
    if s.len() != 1 {
        return Err(format!("Could not convert '{}' to a single ASCII character.", s));
    }
    let b = s.as_bytes()[0];
    if b > 127 {
        return Err(format!("Could not convert '{}' to a single ASCII character.", s));
    }
    Ok(b)
}

fn parse_delim_opt(s: &str, flag_name: &str) -> u8 {
    match parse_delim(s) {
        Ok(d) => d,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("{}", e);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }
}

    while i < len {
        let c = data[i];
        if in_quote {
            if let Some(esc) = escape {
                if c == esc {
                    if i+1 < len {
                        field.push(data[i+1]);
                        i+=2;
                        at_start_of_field = false;

                    } else {
                        field.push(c);
                        i+=1;
                        at_start_of_field = false;

                } else if c == quote {
                    if escape.is_none() {
                        if i+1 < len && data[i+1]==quote {
                            field.push(quote);
                            i+=2;
                            at_start_of_field = false;
                            continue;
                        } else {
                            in_quote = false;
                            i+=1;
                            at_start_of_field = false;
                            continue;
                        }
                    } else {
                        in_quote = false;
                        i+=1;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                } else {
                    field.push(c);
                    i+=1;
                    at_start_of_field = false;
                    continue;
                }
            } else {
                if c == quote {
                    if i+1 < len && data[i+1]==quote {
                        field.push(quote);
                        i+=2;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    } else {
                        in_quote = false;
                        i+=1;
                        at_start_of_field = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                } else {
                    field.push(c);
                    i+=1;
                    at_start_of_field = false;
                    continue;
                }
            }
        } else {
            if quoting && at_start_of_field && c == quote {
                in_quote = true;

                continue;
            }
            if c == delimiter {
                let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&field).into_owned();
                record.push(s);
                field.clear();
                at_start_of_field = true;
                i+=1;
                continue;
            }
            if c == b'\n' {
                let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&field).into_owned();
                record.push(s);
                field.clear();
                // push record
                // Avoid pushing empty record if file is empty? But we'll push if record not empty or field not empty? Actually we need to decide.
                // For offset tracking, after newline, next record starts at i+1
                records.push(record.clone());
                record.clear();
                // next offset
                let next_off = (i+1) as u64;
                if next_off < len as u64 {
                    offsets.push(next_off);
                }
                at_start_of_field = true;
                i+=1;
                continue;
            }
            if c == b'\r' {
                // check \n
                let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&field).into_owned();
                record.push(s);
                field.clear();
                records.push(record.clone());
                record.clear();
                i+=1;
                if i < len && data[i]==b'\n' {
                    i+=1;
                }
                let next_off = i as u64;
                if next_off < len as u64 {
                    offsets.push(next_off);
                }
                at_start_of_field = true;
                continue;
            }
            field.push(c);
            i+=1;

    }
    // EOF

        let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&field).into_owned();

        // If file ends with newline, we already pushed record and offset for next (if any). So records length is number of lines.
        // If file is empty, records is empty, offsets = [0].

    // For empty file, we want offsets = [0] per observed.

    // For file "a,b\n": records = [["a","b"]], offsets = [0] (since next_off =1 which equals len=4? Actually len=4, next_off=4, not < len, so not pushed). So offsets = [0]. But we need offsets for each record: for N records, we need N offsets. For "a,b\n" N=1 offset [0] works.

    Ok((records, offsets))
}

fn write_csv_record<W: Write>(writer: &mut W, fields: &[String], out_delim: u8, quote: u8, quote_always: bool, escape: Option<u8>, crlf: bool, ascii: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
    // ascii overrides delimiter and terminator?
    // According to spec: --ascii uses \x1F as field sep and \x1E as record sep.
    // From earlier od: fmt --ascii produced \x1F between fields, \x1E as record separator.
    // Indeed: "h1\x1Fh2\x1Fh3\x1Ea\x1Fb\x1Fc\x1E..."
    // So when ascii flag set, out_delim is 0x1F, record terminator 0x1E.
    // Quote handling with ascii? Our od showed quote-always with ascii produced quoted fields still with \x1F and \x1E inside? Actually earlier ascii with quote-always gave: 22 68 31 22 1f ... So fields quoted with ", then delimiter 0x1F etc.
    // So implement.

    let field_sep = if ascii { 0x1F } else { out_delim };
    let record_sep = if ascii { 0x1E } else { b'\n' };

    for (idx, field) in fields.iter().enumerate() {
        if idx > 0 {
            writer.write_all(&[field_sep])?;
        }
        // Determine if need quoting
        let needs_quote = if quote_always {
            true
        } else {
            // Need quote if field contains delimiter, quote, newline, \r, or if ascii? Check: ascii doesn't require quoting unless field contains sep or quote etc?
            // Also if field contains out_delim, quote, \r, \n, etc.
            let bytes = field.as_bytes();
            let mut need = false;
            for &b in bytes {
                if b == out_delim && !ascii { need = true; break; }
                if b == field_sep { need = true; break; }
                if b == record_sep { need = true; break; }
                if b == quote { need = true; break; }
                if b == b'\n' || b == b'\r' { need = true; break; }
            }
            need
        };

        if needs_quote {
            writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
            // escape
            for &b in field.as_bytes() {
                if b == quote {
                    if let Some(esc) = escape {
                        writer.write_all(&[esc])?;
                        writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
                    } else {
                        // double quote
                        writer.write_all(&[quote, quote])?;
                    }
                } else {
                    writer.write_all(&[b])?;
                }
            }
            writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
        } else {
            writer.write_all(field.as_bytes())?;
        }
    }
    if crlf && !ascii {
        writer.write_all(b"\r\n")?;
    } else {
        writer.write_all(&[record_sep])?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn csv_writer_from_path(path_opt: Option<&str>) -> Box<dyn Write> {
    if let Some(p) = path_opt {
        let f = File::create(p).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
            eprintln!("failed to open {}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", p);
            std::process::exit(1);
        });
        Box::new(BufWriter::new(f))
    } else {
        Box::new(BufWriter::new(io::stdout()))
    }
}

// Delimiter parsing
fn parse_delim(s: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
    if s.len() != 1 {
        return Err(format!("Could not convert '{}' to a single ASCII character.", s));
    }
    let b = s.as_bytes()[0];
    if b > 127 {
        return Err(format!("Could not convert '{}' to a single ASCII character.", s));
    }
    Ok(b)
}

fn parse_delim_opt(s: &str, flag_name: &str) -> u8 {
    match parse_delim(s) {
        Ok(d) => d,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("{}", e);
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }
}

// ---------------- CSV utilities ----------------

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
struct CsvConfig {
    delimiter: u8,
    quote: u8,
    escape: Option<u8>,
    quoting: bool,
}

impl CsvConfig {
    fn new(delimiter: u8) -> Self {
        Self { delimiter, quote: b'"', escape: None, quoting: true }
    }
}

fn parse_delim(s: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
    if s.chars().count() != 1 {
        return Err(format!("Could not convert '{}' to a single ASCII character.", s));
    }
    let b = s.as_bytes()[0];
    if b > 127 {
        return Err(format!("Could not convert '{}' to a single ASCII character.", s));
    }
    Ok(b)
}

fn read_all_bytes<R: Read>(mut r: R) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    r.read_to_end(&mut buf).unwrap();
    buf
}

fn is_blank_line(line: &[u8]) -> bool {
    line.is_empty()
}

                if c == b'\n' {

                let rec_no = non_blank_line_no - 1;

                let line_no = non_blank_line_no;

            }
        } else {
            first_len = Some(rec_fields.len());
        }

        records.push(rec_fields);
        offsets.push(rec_offset_for_index);
        pending_blank_start = None;
        idx = p;
    }

    Ok(ParsedCsv { records, offsets })

fn write_csv<W: Write>(writer: &mut W, records: &[Vec<String>], out_delim: u8, quote: u8, quote_always: bool, escape: Option<u8>, crlf: bool, ascii: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
    for rec in records {
        write_csv_record(writer, rec, out_delim, quote, quote_always, escape, crlf, ascii)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn write_csv_record<W: Write>(writer: &mut W, fields: &[String], out_delim: u8, quote: u8, quote_always: bool, escape: Option<u8>, crlf: bool, ascii: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
    let field_sep = if ascii { 0x1F } else { out_delim };
    let rec_sep = if ascii { 0x1E } else { b'\n' };

    for (i, f) in fields.iter().enumerate() {
        if i>0 {
            writer.write_all(&[field_sep])?;
        }
        let need_quote = if quote_always {
            true
        } else {
            let bytes = f.as_bytes();
            let mut need = false;
            for &b in bytes {
                if b == field_sep || b == rec_sep || b == quote || b == b'\n' || b == b'\r' {
                    need = true; break;
                }
                if !ascii && b == out_delim {
                    need = true; break;
                }
            }
            need
        };
        if need_quote {
            writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
            for &b in f.as_bytes() {
                if b == quote {
                    if let Some(esc) = escape {
                        writer.write_all(&[esc])?;
                        writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
                    } else {
                        writer.write_all(&[quote, quote])?;
                    }
                } else {
                    writer.write_all(&[b])?;
                }
            }
            writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
        } else {
            writer.write_all(f.as_bytes())?;
        }
    }
    if crlf && !ascii {
        writer.write_all(b"\r\n")?;
    } else {
        writer.write_all(&[rec_sep])?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn open_output(path_opt: Option<String>) -> Box<dyn Write> {
    if let Some(p) = path_opt {
        match File::create(&p) {
            Ok(f) => Box::new(BufWriter::new(f)),
            Err(_) => {
                eprintln!("failed to open {}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", p);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    } else {
        Box::new(BufWriter::new(io::stdout()))
    }
}

// Index reading
struct Index {
    offsets: Vec<u64>,
    count: u64, // total records
}

fn read_index(csv_path: &str) -> Option<Index> {
    let idx_path = format!("{}.idx", csv_path);
    let data = std::fs::read(&idx_path).ok()?;
    if data.len() % 8 != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut vals: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();
    for chunk in data.chunks(8) {
        let mut arr = [0u8;8];
        arr.copy_from_slice(chunk);
        vals.push(u64::from_be_bytes(arr));
    }
    if vals.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    if vals.len() == 1 {
        // empty file
        return Some(Index { offsets: vec![0], count: 0 });
    } else {
        let count = *vals.last().unwrap();
        let offs = vals[..vals.len()-1].to_vec();
        Some(Index { offsets: offs, count })
    }
}

fn check_stale(csv_path: &str) -> bool {
    // returns true if stale (csv mtime sec > idx mtime sec)
    let idx_path = format!("{}.idx", csv_path);
    let csv_meta = std::fs::metadata(csv_path);
    let idx_meta = std::fs::metadata(&idx_path);
    if let (Ok(c), Ok(i)) = (csv_meta, idx_meta) {
        if let (Ok(c_time), Ok(i_time)) = (c.modified(), i.modified()) {
            if let (Ok(c_dur), Ok(i_dur)) = (c_time.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH), i_time.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)) {
                let c_sec = c_dur.as_secs();
                let i_sec = i_dur.as_secs();
                if c_sec > i_sec {
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    false
}

fn ensure_index_not_stale(csv_path: &str) {
    let idx_path = format!("{}.idx", csv_path);
    if Path::new(&idx_path).exists() {
        if check_stale(csv_path) {
            eprintln!("The CSV file was modified after the index file. Please re-create the index.");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }
}

fn cmd_headers(args: &[String]) {
    // Usage: xsv headers [options] [<input>...]
    let mut delimiter = b',';
    let mut just_names = false;
    let mut intersect = false;
    let mut inputs: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut i=0;
    while i<args.len() {
        let a = &args[i];
        if a=="-h"||a=="--help" {
            print!("{}", HELP_HEADERS);
            return;
        } else if a=="-j"||a=="--just-names" {
            just_names = true;
        } else if a=="--intersect" {
            intersect = true;
        } else if a=="-d"||a=="--delimiter" {
            i+=1;
            if i>=args.len() { eprintln!("Invalid arguments.\n\nUsage:\n    {}", "xsv headers [options] [<input>...]"); std::process::exit(1); }
            match parse_delim(&args[i]) {
                Ok(d) => delimiter = d,
                Err(e) => { eprintln!("{}", e); std::process::exit(1); }
            }
        } else if a.starts_with("-") {
            if a.starts_with("-d") && a.len()>2 {
                let val = &a[2..];
                match parse_delim(val) { Ok(d)=>delimiter=d, Err(e)=>{eprintln!("{}", e); std::process::exit(1);} }
            } else if a.starts_with("--delimiter=") {
                let val = &a["--delimiter=".len()..];
                match parse_delim(val) { Ok(d)=>delimiter=d, Err(e)=>{eprintln!("{}", e); std::process::exit(1);} }
            } else {
                eprintln!("Unknown flag: '{}'\n\nUsage:\n    {}", a, "xsv headers [options] [<input>...]");
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        } else {
            inputs.push(a.clone());
        }
        i+=1;
    }

    let cfg = CsvConfig { delimiter, quote: b'"', escape: None, quoting: true };

    if inputs.is_empty() {
        // stdin
        let data = read_input_bytes(None);
        match parse_csv_with_blank_handling(&data, &cfg) {
            Ok(parsed) => {
                if parsed.records.is_empty() {
                    // no headers
                    return;
                }
                let header = &parsed.records[0];
                if just_names {
                    for h in header {
                        println!("{}", h);
                    }
                } else {
                    for (idx, h) in header.iter().enumerate() {
                        println!("{}\t{}", idx+1, h);
                    }
                }
            },
            Err(msg) => {
                eprintln!("CSV error: {}", msg);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
        return;
    }

    // multiple files
    let mut all_headers: Vec<Vec<String>> = Vec::new();
    for path in &inputs {
        let data = if path=="-" {
            let mut buf=Vec::new();
            io::stdin().read_to_end(&mut buf).unwrap();
            buf
        } else {
            match std::fs::read(path) {
                Ok(b)=>b,
                Err(_) => { eprintln!("failed to open {}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", path); std::process::exit(1); }
            }
        };
        match parse_csv_with_blank_handling(&data, &cfg) {
            Ok(parsed) => {
                if parsed.records.is_empty() {
                    all_headers.push(vec![]);
                } else {
                    all_headers.push(parsed.records[0].clone());
                }
            },
            Err(msg) => {
                eprintln!("CSV error: {}", msg);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    }

    if intersect {
        if all_headers.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        // intersection of all headers, preserving order of first
        let first = &all_headers[0];
        let mut result: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        let mut seen: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
        for h in first {
            if seen.contains(h) { continue; }
            let mut in_all = true;
            for other in all_headers.iter().skip(1) {
                if !other.contains(h) {
                    in_all = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if in_all {
                seen.insert(h.clone());
                result.push(h.clone());
            }
        }
        for h in result {
            println!("{}", h);
        }
    } else {
        if inputs.len() > 1 {
            // auto just-names
            for headers in all_headers {
                for h in headers {
                    println!("{}", h);
                }
            }
        } else {
            let header = &all_headers[0];
            if just_names {
                for h in header {
                    println!("{}", h);
                }
            } else {
                for (idx, h) in header.iter().enumerate() {
                    println!("{}\t{}", idx+1, h);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn split_selectors(s: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut tokens: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut cur = String::new();
    let mut in_quote = false;
    let mut i = 0;
    let bytes = s.as_bytes();
    while i < bytes.len() {
        let c = bytes[i] as char;
        if c == '"' {
            if in_quote {
                if i+1 < bytes.len() && bytes[i+1]==b'"' as u8 {
                    // escaped quote
                    cur.push('"');
                    cur.push('"');
                    i+=2;
                    continue;
                } else {
                    in_quote = false;
                    cur.push(c);
                    i+=1;
                    continue;
                }
            } else {
                in_quote = true;
                cur.push(c);
                i+=1;
                continue;
            }
        }
        if c == ',' && !in_quote {
            tokens.push(cur);
            cur = String::new();
            i+=1;
            continue;
        }
        cur.push(c);
        i+=1;
    }
    tokens.push(cur);
    tokens
}

// split range: find '-' outside quotes and outside []
fn split_range(token: &str) -> Option<(String, Option<String>)> {
    // Returns (left, Some(right)) if '-' found, where right may be empty (open-ended)
    // Returns None if no range separator
    let bytes = token.as_bytes();
    let mut in_quote = false;
    let mut in_bracket = false;
    for (i, &b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
        if b == b'"' {
            if in_quote {
                if i+1 < bytes.len() && bytes[i+1]==b'"' {
                    // skip escaped
                    // we need to skip next char as well? But for range detection, we can just toggle? Simpler: if in_quote and next is quote, skip both
                    // We'll handle in loop with manual index, but for simplicity, we treat "" as not closing
                    continue;
                } else {
                    in_quote = false;
                }
            } else {
                in_quote = true;
            }
        } else if b == b'[' && !in_quote {
            in_bracket = true;
        } else if b == b']' && !in_quote {
            in_bracket = false;
        } else if b == b'-' && !in_quote && !in_bracket {
            // found separator
            let left = token[..i].to_string();
            let right = token[i+1..].to_string();
            return Some((left, Some(right)));
        }
    }
    None
}

fn resolve_item(item: &str, headers: &[String], num_cols: usize, no_headers: bool) -> Vec<usize> {
    // item may be like '"a,b"' or 'a' or '1' or 'a[0]' or '"a"[1]'
    // Extract base and optional [n]
    let (base, idx_opt) = extract_bracket(item);

    // Determine if base is numeric
    let is_numeric = base.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) && !base.is_empty();

    if is_numeric {
        if idx_opt.is_some() {
            // treat as name lookup for numeric string with index -> will fail as name not found
            // So we go to name lookup path
        } else {
            // numeric index
            match base.parse::<usize>() {
                Ok(n) => {
                    if n==0 {
                        eprintln!("Selector index 0 is out of bounds. Index must be >= 1 and <= {}.", num_cols);
                        std::process::exit(1);
                    }
                    if n > num_cols {
                        eprintln!("Selector index {} is out of bounds. Index must be >= 1 and <= {}.", n, num_cols);
                        std::process::exit(1);
                    }
                    return vec![n-1];
                },
                Err(_) => {
                    // should not happen
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Name lookup
    if no_headers {
        eprintln!("Cannot use names ('{}') in selection with --no-headers set.", base);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }

    // For name, need to handle quoted names: base may be like "\"a,b\"" or "\"a\""
    let name = if base.starts_with('"') && base.ends_with('"') && base.len()>=2 {
        // unescape double quotes: "" -> "
        let inner = &base[1..base.len()-1];
        inner.replace("\"\"", "\"")
    } else {
        base.clone()
    };

    // Find all indices where header == name
    let mut matches: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    for (i, h) in headers.iter().enumerate() {
        if h == &name {
            matches.push(i);
        }
    }

    if matches.is_empty() {
        eprintln!("Selector name '{}' does not exist as a named header in the given CSV data.", name);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }

    if let Some(idx_str) = idx_opt {
        match idx_str.parse::<usize>() {
            Ok(n) => {
                if n >= matches.len() {
                    eprintln!("Selector index '{}' for name '{}' is out of bounds. Must be >= 0 and <= {}.", n, name, matches.len()-1);
                    std::process::exit(1);
                }
                return vec![matches[n]];
            },
            Err(_) => {
                eprintln!("Selector name '{}' does not exist as a named header in the given CSV data.", name);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Without index, return first match? Or all? Original seems to return first only.
        // For duplicates, bare name returns first.
        return vec![matches[0]];
    }
}

fn extract_bracket(item: &str) -> (String, Option<String>) {
    // Find last '[' and check ends with ']'
    if let Some(start) = item.rfind('[') {
        if item.ends_with(']') {
            let base = item[..start].to_string();
            let idx = item[start+1..item.len()-1].to_string();
            // Ensure idx is digits only
            if idx.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
                return (base, Some(idx));
            }
        }
    }
    (item.to_string(), None)
}

                regex_str=Some(a.clone());
            } else if input.is_none() {
                input=Some(a.clone());
            } else {
                eprintln!("Invalid arguments.\n\nUsage:\n    {}", "xsv search [options] <regex> [<input>]\n    xsv search --help");
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
        i+=1;
    }
    if regex_str.is_none() {
        eprintln!("Invalid arguments.\n\nUsage:\n    {}", "xsv search [options] <regex> [<input>]\n    xsv search --help");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
    let mut re_str = regex_str.unwrap();
    if ignore_case {
        if !re_str.starts_with("(?i)") {
            re_str = format!("(?i){}", re_str);
        }
    }
    let re = match regex::Regex::new(&re_str) {
        Ok(r)=>r,
        Err(e)=>{ eprintln!("{}", e); std::process::exit(1); }
    };

    let cfg = CsvConfig { delimiter, quote: b'"', escape: None, quoting: true };
    if let Some(ref path) = input {
        if path!="-" {
            let idx_path = format!("{}.idx", path);
            if Path::new(&idx_path).exists() && check_stale(path) {
                eprintln!("The CSV file was modified after the index file. Please re-create the index.");
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    }
    let data = read_input_bytes(input);
    let parsed = match parse_csv_with_blank_handling(&data, &cfg) {
        Ok(p)=>p,
        Err(msg)=>{ eprintln!("CSV error: {}", msg); std::process::exit(1); }
    };

    if parsed.records.is_empty() { return; }

    let headers = if no_headers { vec![] } else { parsed.records[0].clone() };
    let data_recs = if no_headers { parsed.records.clone() } else { parsed.records[1..].to_vec() };

    let num_cols = if no_headers {
        if parsed.records.is_empty() {0} else { parsed.records[0].len() }
    } else { headers.len() };

    // Determine columns to search
    let mut search_indices: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    if let Some(sel_str) = select {
        // parse select similar to before
        let (invert_sel, sel_inner) = if sel_str.starts_with('!') {
            (true, sel_str[1..].to_string())
        } else {
            (false, sel_str.clone())
        };
        let mut sel_idxs: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
        if !sel_inner.is_empty() {
            let tokens = split_selectors(&sel_inner);
            for token in tokens {
                if token.is_empty() { continue; }
                if let Some((left, right_opt)) = split_range(&token) {
                    if left.is_empty() { eprintln!("Expected end of field but got '-' instead."); std::process::exit(1); }
                    let left_res = resolve_item(&left, &headers, num_cols, no_headers);
                    let left_idx = left_res[0];
                    if let Some(right) = right_opt {
                        if right.is_empty() {
                            for idx in left_idx..num_cols { sel_idxs.push(idx); }
                        } else {
                            let right_res = resolve_item(&right, &headers, num_cols, no_headers);
                            let right_idx = right_res[0];
                            if left_idx <= right_idx {
                                for idx in left_idx..=right_idx { sel_idxs.push(idx); }
                            } else {
                                for idx in (right_idx..=left_idx).rev() { sel_idxs.push(idx); }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                } else {
                    let mut idxs = resolve_item(&token, &headers, num_cols, no_headers);
                    sel_idxs.append(&mut idxs);
                }
            }
        }
        if invert_sel {
            let set: HashSet<usize> = sel_idxs.into_iter().collect();
            search_indices = (0..num_cols).filter(|i| !set.contains(i)).collect();
        } else {
            search_indices = sel_idxs;
        }
    } else {
        search_indices = (0..num_cols).collect();
    }

    let mut writer = open_output(output);
    // Write header if present
    if !no_headers {
        write_csv_record(&mut writer, &headers, b',', b'"', false, None, false, false).unwrap();
    }
    for rec in data_recs {
        let mut matched = false;
        for &col in &search_indices {
            if col < rec.len() {
                if re.is_match(&rec[col]) {
                    matched = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        let should_output = if invert { !matched } else { matched };
        if should_output {
            write_csv_record(&mut writer, &rec, b',', b'"', false, None, false, false).unwrap();
        }
    }
}

    }

    let cfg = CsvConfig { delimiter, quote: b'"', escape: None, quoting: true };
    let data = read_input_bytes(input);
    let parsed = match parse_csv_with_blank_handling(&data, &cfg) {
        Ok(p)=>p,
        Err(msg)=>{ eprintln!("CSV error: {}", msg); std::process::exit(1); }
    };

    if parsed.records.is_empty() { return; }

    let headers = if no_headers { vec![] } else { parsed.records[0].clone() };
    let mut data_recs = if no_headers { parsed.records.clone() } else { parsed.records[1..].to_vec() };

    let num_cols = if no_headers {
        if parsed.records.is_empty() {0} else { parsed.records[0].len() }
    } else { headers.len() };

    // Determine sort columns
    let mut sort_indices: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    if let Some(sel_str) = select {
        // parse select, handling inversion
        let (inv, inner) = if sel_str.starts_with('!') { (true, sel_str[1..].to_string()) } else { (false, sel_str.clone()) };
        let mut sel_idxs: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
        if !inner.is_empty() {
            let tokens = split_selectors(&inner);
            for token in tokens {
                if token.is_empty() { continue; }
                if let Some((left, right_opt)) = split_range(&token) {
                    if left.is_empty() { eprintln!("Expected end of field but got '-' instead."); std::process::exit(1); }
                    let left_res = resolve_item(&left, &headers, num_cols, no_headers);
                    let left_idx = left_res[0];
                    if let Some(right) = right_opt {
                        if right.is_empty() {
                            for idx in left_idx..num_cols { sel_idxs.push(idx); }
                        } else {
                            let right_res = resolve_item(&right, &headers, num_cols, no_headers);
                            let right_idx = right_res[0];
                            if left_idx <= right_idx {
                                for idx in left_idx..=right_idx { sel_idxs.push(idx); }
                            } else {
                                for idx in (right_idx..=left_idx).rev() { sel_idxs.push(idx); }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                } else {
                    let mut idxs = resolve_item(&token, &headers, num_cols, no_headers);
                    sel_idxs.append(&mut idxs);
                }
            }
        }
        if inv {
            let set: HashSet<usize> = sel_idxs.into_iter().collect();
            sort_indices = (0..num_cols).filter(|i| !set.contains(i)).collect();
        } else {
            sort_indices = sel_idxs;
        }
    } else {
        sort_indices = (0..num_cols).collect();
    }

    // Sort
    data_recs.sort_by(|a,b| {
        for &col in &sort_indices {
            let av = if col < a.len() { &a[col] } else { "" };
            let bv = if col < b.len() { &b[col] } else { "" };
            let ord = if numeric {
                // compare as numbers? Try parse as f64
                let an = av.parse::<f64>();
                let bn = bv.parse::<f64>();
                if let (Ok(an), Ok(bn)) = (an, bn) {
                    an.partial_cmp(&bn).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
                } else {
                    av.cmp(bv)
                }
            } else {
                av.cmp(bv)
            };
            if ord != std::cmp::Ordering::Equal {
                return if reverse { ord.reverse() } else { ord };
            }
        }
        std::cmp::Ordering::Equal
    });

    let mut writer = open_output(output);
    if !no_headers {
        write_csv_record(&mut writer, &headers, b',', b'"', false, None, false, false).unwrap();
    }
    for rec in data_recs {
        write_csv_record(&mut writer, &rec, b',', b'"', false, None, false, false).unwrap();
    }
}

                        let m = nums[mid];
                        if m.fract()==0.0 { format!("{}", m as i64) } else { format!("{}", m) }
                    }
                }
            };
            // mode: most frequent value, if tie? Original shows "N/A" if no mode? For integer column with all distinct, mode N/A. For file with duplicate? We haven't tested.
            // For simplicity, compute mode: find value with max count, if multiple with same max count and count>1, pick first? If all distinct, N/A.
            let mode_str = {
                let mut freq: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();
                for v in &st.values {
                    *freq.entry(v.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1;
                }
                if freq.is_empty() {
                    "".to_string()
                } else {
                    let max_c = freq.values().cloned().max().unwrap_or(0);
                    if max_c <=1 {
                        "N/A".to_string()
                    } else {
                        // find first value with max count
                        let mut mode_val = "";
                        for v in &st.values {
                            if freq.get(v).unwrap_or(&0) == &max_c {
                                mode_val = v;
                                break;
                            }
                        }
                        mode_val.to_string()
                    }
                }
            };
            // cardinality: distinct count
            let card_str = {
                let mut set = HashSet::new();
                for v in &st.values { set.insert(v); }
                set.len().to_string()
            };
            out_rec.push(median_str);
            out_rec.push(mode_str);
            out_rec.push(card_str);
        } else {
            if median {
                let median_str = if st.values.is_empty() { "".to_string() } else {
                    let mut nums: Vec<f64> = st.values.iter().filter_map(|v| v.parse::<f64>().ok()).collect();
                    if nums.is_empty() { "".to_string() } else {
                        nums.sort_by(|a,b| a.partial_cmp(b).unwrap());
                        let mid = nums.len()/2;
                        if nums.len()%2==0 {
                            let m = (nums[mid-1]+nums[mid])/2.0;
                            if m.fract()==0.0 { format!("{}", m as i64) } else { format!("{}", m) }
                        } else {
                            let m = nums[mid];
                            if m.fract()==0.0 { format!("{}", m as i64) } else { format!("{}", m) }
                        }
                    }
                };
                out_rec.push(median_str);
            }
            if show_mode {
                let mode_str = {
                    let mut freq: HashMap<String, usize> = HashMap::new();
                    for v in &st.values { *freq.entry(v.clone()).or_insert(0) += 1; }
                    if freq.is_empty() { "".to_string() } else {
                        let max_c = freq.values().cloned().max().unwrap_or(0);
                        if max_c <=1 { "N/A".to_string() } else {
                            let mut mode_val = "";
                            for v in &st.values {
                                if freq.get(v).unwrap_or(&0) == &max_c {
                                    mode_val = v;
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                            mode_val.to_string()
                        }
                    }
                };
                out_rec.push(mode_str);
            }
            if cardinality {
                let mut set = HashSet::new();
                for v in &st.values { set.insert(v); }
                out_rec.push(set.len().to_string());
            }
        }

        write_csv_record(&mut writer, &out_rec, b',', b'"', false, None, false, false).unwrap();
    }
}

fn parse_join_columns(sel_str: &str, headers: &[String], num_cols: usize, no_headers: bool) -> Vec<usize> {
    // Similar to select parsing but without inversion and without open-ended? Actually join columns can be ranges? The help says columns can be referenced by name or index, range with '-'.
    // We'll parse using same split and range logic as select, but no invert.

    let mut result: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    let tokens = split_selectors(sel_str);
    for token in tokens {
        if token.is_empty() { continue; }
        if let Some((left, right_opt)) = split_range(&token) {
            if left.is_empty() { eprintln!("Expected end of field but got '-' instead."); std::process::exit(1); }
            let left_res = resolve_item(&left, headers, num_cols, no_headers);
            let left_idx = left_res[0];
            if let Some(right) = right_opt {
                if right.is_empty() {
                    for idx in left_idx..num_cols { result.push(idx); }
                } else {
                    let right_res = resolve_item(&right, headers, num_cols, no_headers);
                    let right_idx = right_res[0];
                    if left_idx <= right_idx {
                        for idx in left_idx..=right_idx { result.push(idx); }
                    } else {
                        for idx in (right_idx..=left_idx).rev() { result.push(idx); }
                    }
                }
            }
        } else {
            let mut idxs = resolve_item(&token, headers, num_cols, no_headers);
            result.append(&mut idxs);
        }
    }
    result
}

fn cmd_partition(args: &[String]) {

        else if a=="-n"||a=="--no-headers" { no_headers=true; }
        else if a=="--drop" { drop=true; }

        } else if a.starts_with("--prefix-length=") {
            let val=&a["--prefix-length=".len()..];
            match val.parse::<usize>() { Ok(v)=>prefix_len=Some(v), Err(_) => { eprintln!("Could not deserialize '{}' to u64 for '--prefix-length'.", val); std::process::exit(1); } }
        } else if a.starts_with("-p") && a.len()>2 {
            let val=&a[2..];
            match val.parse::<usize>() { Ok(v)=>prefix_len=Some(v), Err(_) => { eprintln!("Could not deserialize '{}' to u64 for '--prefix-length'.", val); std::process::exit(1); } }
        } else if a=="--filename" {
            i+=1;
            if i>=args.len() { eprintln!("Invalid arguments.\n\nUsage:\n    {}", "xsv partition [options] <column> <outdir> [<input>]\n    xsv partition --help"); std::process::exit(1); }
            filename_template=args[i].clone();
        } else if a.starts_with("--filename=") {
            filename_template=a["--filename=".len()..].to_string();
        } else if a=="-d"||a=="--delimiter" {
            i+=1;
            if i>=args.len() { eprintln!("Invalid arguments.\n\nUsage:\n    {}", "xsv partition [options] <column> <outdir> [<input>]\n    xsv partition --help"); std::process::exit(1); }
            match parse_delim(&args[i]) { Ok(d)=>delimiter=d, Err(e)=>{eprintln!("{}", e); std::process::exit(1);} }
        } else if a.starts_with("-d") && a.len()>2 {
            let val=&a[2..];
            match parse_delim(val) { Ok(d)=>delimiter=d, Err(e)=>{eprintln!("{}", e); std::process::exit(1);} }
        } else if a.starts_with("--delimiter=") {
            let val=&a["--delimiter=".len()..];
            match parse_delim(val) { Ok(d)=>delimiter=d, Err(e)=>{eprintln!("{}", e); std::process::exit(1);} }
        } else if a.starts_with("-") {
            eprintln!("Unknown flag: '{}'\n\nUsage:\n    {}", a, "xsv partition [options] <column> <outdir> [<input>]\n    xsv partition --help");
            std::process::exit(1);
        } else {
            if column.is_none() { column=Some(a.clone()); }
            else if outdir.is_none() { outdir=Some(a.clone()); }
            else if input.is_none() { input=Some(a.clone()); }
            else { eprintln!("Invalid arguments.\n\nUsage:\n    {}", "xsv partition [options] <column> <outdir> [<input>]\n    xsv partition --help"); std::process::exit(1); }
        }
        i+=1;
    }

    if column.is_none() || outdir.is_none() {
        eprintln!("Invalid arguments.\n\nUsage:\n    {}", "xsv partition [options] <column> <outdir> [<input>]\n    xsv partition --help");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }

    if !filename_template.contains("{}") {
        eprintln!("The --filename argument must contain one '{{}}'.");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }

    let col_str = column.unwrap();
    let outdir_str = outdir.unwrap();

    let cfg = CsvConfig { delimiter, quote: b'"', escape: None, quoting: true };
    let data = read_input_bytes(input);
    let parsed = match parse_csv_with_blank_handling(&data, &cfg) {
        Ok(p)=>p,
        Err(msg)=>{ eprintln!("CSV error: {}", msg); std::process::exit(1); }
    };

    if parsed.records.is_empty() { return; }

    let headers = if no_headers { vec![] } else { parsed.records[0].clone() };
    let data_recs = if no_headers { parsed.records.clone() } else { parsed.records[1..].to_vec() };

    let num_cols = if no_headers {
        if parsed.records.is_empty() {0} else { parsed.records[0].len() }
    } else { headers.len() };

    // Resolve column
    let col_idx = {
        let mut idxs = parse_join_columns(&col_str, &headers, num_cols, no_headers);
        if idxs.is_empty() { eprintln!("Invalid arguments.\n\nUsage:\n    {}", "xsv partition [options] <column> <outdir> [<input>]\n    xsv partition --help"); std::process::exit(1); }
        idxs[0]
    };

    std::fs::create_dir_all(&outdir_str).unwrap_or_else(|_| {
        eprintln!("failed to open {}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", outdir_str);
        std::process::exit(1);
    });

    // Map partition value -> file writer
    struct PartWriter {
        writer: BufWriter<File>,
    }

    let mut writers: HashMap<String, PartWriter> = HashMap::new();

    for rec in data_recs {
        if col_idx >= rec.len() { continue; }
        let mut part_val = rec[col_idx].clone();
        if let Some(pl) = prefix_len {
            if part_val.len() > pl {
                part_val = part_val[..pl].to_string();
            }
        }

        // sanitize for shell safety: replace non-alphanumeric with underscore? Original says sanitized for shell safety.
        // Let's implement simple sanitization: keep alphanumeric, dash, underscore, dot, replace others with underscore.
        // Also need to handle empty?
        let sanitized = sanitize_filename(&part_val);

        let key = sanitized.clone();

        // Determine filename
        let filename = filename_template.replace("{}", &key);
        let full_path = Path::new(&outdir_str).join(&filename);

        // Get writer or create
        if !writers.contains_key(&key) {
            let file = File::create(&full_path).unwrap();
            let mut w = BufWriter::new(file);
            if !no_headers {
                let mut out_header = Vec::new();
                for (i, h) in headers.iter().enumerate() {
                    if drop && i==col_idx { continue; }
                    out_header.push(h.clone());
                }
                write_csv_record(&mut w, &out_header, b',', b'"', false, None, false, false).unwrap();
            }
            writers.insert(key.clone(), PartWriter { writer: w });
        }

        let pw = writers.get_mut(&key).unwrap();
        let mut out_rec: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        for (i, field) in rec.iter().enumerate() {
            if drop && i==col_idx { continue; }
            out_rec.push(field.clone());
        }
        write_csv_record(&mut pw.writer, &out_rec, b',', b'"', false, None, false, false).unwrap();
    }
}

fn sanitize_filename(s: &str) -> String {
    if s.is_empty() {
        return "empty".to_string(); //? Not sure
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    for ch in s.chars() {
        if ch.is_alphanumeric() || ch=='-' || ch=='_' || ch=='.' {
            out.push(ch);
        } else {
            out.push('_');
        }
    }
    out
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]

    delimiter: u8,
    quote: u8,
    escape: Option<u8>,
    quoting: bool,
}

    fn new(delimiter: u8) -> Self {

fn parse_delim(s: &str) -> Result<u8, String> {
    if s.chars().count() != 1 {
        return Err(format!("Could not convert '{}' to a single ASCII character.", s));
    }
    let b = s.as_bytes()[0];
    if b > 127 {
        return Err(format!("Could not convert '{}' to a single ASCII character.", s));
    }
    Ok(b)
}

    buf

        // Not blank at idx, parse a CSV record starting at idx
        let rec_start_actual = idx;
        let rec_offset_for_index = pending_blank_start.unwrap_or(rec_start_actual) as u64;
        let rec_start_for_error_byte = rec_offset_for_index as usize; // use same as index offset

        // Parse one record
        let mut field_buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        let mut rec_fields: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        let mut in_quote = false;
        let mut at_field_start = true;
        let mut p = idx;
        let mut end_of_record = false;

        while p < len {
            let c = data[p];
            if in_quote {
                if let Some(esc) = cfg.escape {
                    if c == esc {
                        if p+1 < len {
                            field_buf.push(data[p+1]);
                            p+=2;
                            at_field_start = false;
                            continue;
                        } else {
                            field_buf.push(c);
                            p+=1;
                            at_field_start = false;
                            continue;
                        }
                    } else if c == cfg.quote {
                        if cfg.escape.is_none() {
                            if p+1 < len && data[p+1]==cfg.quote {
                                field_buf.push(cfg.quote);
                                p+=2;
                                at_field_start = false;
                                continue;
                            } else {
                                in_quote = false;
                                p+=1;
                                at_field_start = false;
                                continue;
                            }
                        } else {
                            in_quote = false;
                            p+=1;
                            at_field_start = false;
                            continue;
                        }
                    } else {
                        field_buf.push(c);
                        p+=1;
                        at_field_start = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                } else {
                    if c == cfg.quote {
                        if p+1 < len && data[p+1]==cfg.quote {
                            field_buf.push(cfg.quote);
                            p+=2;
                            at_field_start = false;
                            continue;
                        } else {
                            in_quote = false;
                            p+=1;
                            at_field_start = false;
                            continue;
                        }
                    } else {
                        field_buf.push(c);
                        p+=1;
                        at_field_start = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                }
            } else {
                if cfg.quoting && at_field_start && c == cfg.quote {
                    in_quote = true;
                    p+=1;
                    at_field_start = false;
                    continue;
                }
                if c == cfg.delimiter {
                    let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&field_buf).into_owned();
                    rec_fields.push(s);
                    field_buf.clear();
                    at_field_start = true;
                    p+=1;
                    continue;
                }
                if c == b'\n' {
                    let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&field_buf).into_owned();
                    rec_fields.push(s);
                    field_buf.clear();
                    p+=1;
                    end_of_record = true;
                    break;
                }
                if c == b'\r' {
                    let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&field_buf).into_owned();
                    rec_fields.push(s);
                    field_buf.clear();
                    p+=1;
                    if p < len && data[p]==b'\n' {
                        p+=1;
                    }
                    end_of_record = true;
                    break;
                }
                field_buf.push(c);
                p+=1;
                at_field_start = false;
                continue;
            }
        }

        // If we reached EOF without newline, we still have a record if field_buf or rec_fields not empty
        if !end_of_record {
            // EOF
            if !field_buf.is_empty() || !rec_fields.is_empty() {
                let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&field_buf).into_owned();
                rec_fields.push(s);
                // final record
            } else {
                // No record, break
                break;
            }
        }

        // Now rec_fields is the parsed record (non-blank)
        // Check if it's actually blank (should have been caught earlier, but if line had spaces? Our blank detection only for 0-byte lines, so line with spaces would have field_buf with spaces, rec_fields ["   "] etc, not blank)
        // For our blank detection, we already handled 0-byte lines. So this rec is non-blank.

        // For index offsets and counting
        non_blank_line_no += 1; // counts this record as a non-blank line
        // first_len check
        if let Some(fl) = first_len {
            if rec_fields.len() != fl {
                // Error
                // record number is non_blank_line_no -1? Since first record is header, data records start at 1. For file with only header, non_blank_line_no=1, no error. For second record, non_blank_line_no=2, record number for error is non_blank_line_no-1? Let's see: file "a,b\n1,2,3\n": header is line1, data is line2, non_blank_line_no for data =2, record number should be 1. So record number = non_blank_line_no -1.
                let rec_no = non_blank_line_no - 1;
                // line number for error: non_blank_line_no? For that file, non_blank_line_no=2, line reported 2, matches.
                let line_no = non_blank_line_no;
                let byte_off = rec_offset_for_index as usize;
                let msg = format!("record {} (line: {}, byte: {}): found record with {} fields, but the previous record has {} fields", rec_no, line_no, byte_off, rec_fields.len(), fl);
                return Err(msg);
            }
        } else {
            first_len = Some(rec_fields.len());
        }

        records.push(rec_fields);
        offsets.push(rec_offset_for_index);
        pending_blank_start = None;
        idx = p;
    }

    Ok(ParsedCsv { records, offsets })
}

fn write_csv<W: Write>(writer: &mut W, records: &[Vec<String>], out_delim: u8, quote: u8, quote_always: bool, escape: Option<u8>, crlf: bool, ascii: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
    for rec in records {
        write_csv_record(writer, rec, out_delim, quote, quote_always, escape, crlf, ascii)?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn write_csv_record<W: Write>(writer: &mut W, fields: &[String], out_delim: u8, quote: u8, quote_always: bool, escape: Option<u8>, crlf: bool, ascii: bool) -> io::Result<()> {
    let field_sep = if ascii { 0x1F } else { out_delim };
    let rec_sep = if ascii { 0x1E } else { b'\n' };

    for (i, f) in fields.iter().enumerate() {
        if i>0 {
            writer.write_all(&[field_sep])?;
        }
        let need_quote = if quote_always {
            true
        } else {
            let bytes = f.as_bytes();
            let mut need = false;
            for &b in bytes {
                if b == field_sep || b == rec_sep || b == quote || b == b'\n' || b == b'\r' {
                    need = true; break;
                }
                if !ascii && b == out_delim {
                    need = true; break;
                }
            }
            need
        };
        if need_quote {
            writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
            for &b in f.as_bytes() {
                if b == quote {
                    if let Some(esc) = escape {
                        writer.write_all(&[esc])?;
                        writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
                    } else {
                        writer.write_all(&[quote, quote])?;
                    }
                } else {
                    writer.write_all(&[b])?;
                }
            }
            writer.write_all(&[quote])?;
        } else {
            writer.write_all(f.as_bytes())?;
        }
    }
    if crlf && !ascii {
        writer.write_all(b"\r\n")?;
    } else {
        writer.write_all(&[rec_sep])?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn open_output(path_opt: Option<String>) -> Box<dyn Write> {
    if let Some(p) = path_opt {
        match File::create(&p) {
            Ok(f) => Box::new(BufWriter::new(f)),
            Err(_) => {
                eprintln!("failed to open {}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", p);
                std::process::exit(1);
            }
        }
    } else {
        Box::new(BufWriter::new(io::stdout()))
    }
}

fn read_input_bytes(input_opt: Option<String>) -> Vec<u8> {
    if let Some(p) = input_opt {
        if p == "-" {
            let mut buf = Vec::new();
            io::stdin().read_to_end(&mut buf).unwrap();
            buf
        } else {
            match std::fs::read(&p) {
                Ok(b) => b,
                Err(_) => {
                    eprintln!("failed to open {}: No such file or directory (os error 2)", p);
                    std::process::exit(1);
                }
            }
        }
    } else {
        let mut buf = Vec::new();
        io::stdin().read_to_end(&mut buf).unwrap();
        buf
    }
}

fn get_output_writer(o: Option<String>) -> Box<dyn Write> {
    open_output(o)
}

// Index reading
struct Index {
    offsets: Vec<u64>,
    count: u64, // total records
}

fn read_index(csv_path: &str) -> Option<Index> {
    let idx_path = format!("{}.idx", csv_path);
    let data = std::fs::read(&idx_path).ok()?;
    if data.len() % 8 != 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let mut vals: Vec<u64> = Vec::new();
    for chunk in data.chunks(8) {
        let mut arr = [0u8;8];
        arr.copy_from_slice(chunk);
        vals.push(u64::from_be_bytes(arr));
    }
    if vals.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    if vals.len() == 1 {
        // empty file
        return Some(Index { offsets: vec![0], count: 0 });
    } else {
        let count = *vals.last().unwrap();
        let offs = vals[..vals.len()-1].to_vec();
        Some(Index { offsets: offs, count })
    }
}

fn check_stale(csv_path: &str) -> bool {
    // returns true if stale (csv mtime sec > idx mtime sec)
    let idx_path = format!("{}.idx", csv_path);
    let csv_meta = std::fs::metadata(csv_path);
    let idx_meta = std::fs::metadata(&idx_path);
    if let (Ok(c), Ok(i)) = (csv_meta, idx_meta) {
        if let (Ok(c_time), Ok(i_time)) = (c.modified(), i.modified()) {
            if let (Ok(c_dur), Ok(i_dur)) = (c_time.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH), i_time.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)) {
                let c_sec = c_dur.as_secs();
                let i_sec = i_dur.as_secs();
                if c_sec > i_sec {
                    return true;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    false
}

fn ensure_index_not_stale(csv_path: &str) {
    let idx_path = format!("{}.idx", csv_path);
    if Path::new(&idx_path).exists() {
        if check_stale(csv_path) {
            eprintln!("The CSV file was modified after the index file. Please re-create the index.");
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
    }
}
